name: US Census Bureau API (ACS, Decennial, Population Estimates)
description: Every published Census table queryable by geography, from the nation down to the block group - population, income, housing, commuting, language, ancestry and several hundred other variables in the American Community Survey alone. The definitive denominator for any US per-capita statistic.

access.auth_note: a free key from api.census.gov/data/key_signup.html. Keyless requests are no longer served - see the gotcha, the failure is silent.
access.rate_limit: 500 calls/day per key without registration limits published beyond that
access.pagination: none - you widen or narrow the geography instead

fields: get= comma-separated variable ids, e.g. B01001_001E (total population)

probes.description: The exact call every tutorial shows, without a key
probes.known_broken: Since some point before 2026-09-06 a keyless call 302s to https://api.census.gov/data/missing_key.html, which answers 200 with an HTML page. A client that follows redirects and does not check content-type sees a successful request and a JSON parse error.

recipes.title: Population by county for one state
recipes.code:
KEY=your_key_here
curl -s "https://api.census.gov/data/2023/acs/acs5?get=NAME,B01001_001E&for=county:*&in=state:24&key=$KEY" | head -5
# Response is an array of arrays; row 0 is the header.

gotchas.trap: A missing key does not return 401. It returns a 302 to an HTML 'Missing Key' page that answers 200, so the failure surfaces as a JSON decode error in your own code.
gotchas.fix: Check content-type, or assert the body starts with '[['.

gotchas.trap: The response is an array of arrays with the header in row 0, not an array of objects.
gotchas.fix: rows = json.load(...); dict(zip(rows[0], r)) for r in rows[1:].

gotchas.trap: ACS 5-year and 1-year tables have the same variable ids but different geographies and margins of error.
gotchas.fix: 1-year covers only areas above 65,000 population. For counties and tracts you almost always want acs5.
